# Incident Report — MTA 2026-01-31 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Evidence Reviewed
- `2026-01-31-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (51,181 packets, 26 MB, capture window 2026-01-28 03:04:03–03:14:27 UTC, ~624s). No IDS/Suricata alert export or other artifacts were present in the evidence directory — attribution below is behavioral, based solely on tshark analysis of this capture.

## Victim Host
| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | **10.1.21.58** | DHCP lease, all suspicious traffic source |
| MAC | **00:21:5d:c8:0e:f2** (Intel) | ARP replies for 10.1.21.58, bound to DHCP Discover/Request frames |
| Hostname | **DESKTOP-ES9F3ML** | DHCP option 12 (frames 1/3), NBNS name registrations |
| Workgroup/domain NetBIOS name | WIN11OFFICE | NBNS `<1e>` Browser Election registration |
| Logged-in domain user | **WIN11OFFICE\gwyatt** | Kerberos `CNameString=gwyatt`, realm `WIN11OFFICE.COM`, in AS exchanges between 10.1.21.58 and the domain controller 10.1.21.2 |

Domain controller for context: `WIN-LU4L24X3UB7.win11office.com` at 10.1.21.2, MAC 14:b3:1f:2d:ce:69 — confirmed via SRV lookup (`_ldap._tcp...win11office.com` → 10.1.21.2) and SMB2 tree connects to `\\WIN-LU4L24X3UB7\IPC$` and `\\WIN-LU4L24X3UB7\Shared`. This is the legitimate DC, not the attacker.

## Malware Family
**Attribution: behavioral, not signature-confirmed** (no IDS export in evidence, and the actual payload could not be recovered because its download was TLS-encrypted with Encrypted Client Hello — no session keys available).

Behavior observed is consistent with a **fake-file-host / "ClickFix"-style stealer-loader delivery chain** (the pattern widely associated with Lumma Stealer-style malvertising TDS campaigns):

1. **Lure/redirect** — 10.1.21.58 resolves and connects to `hiyter.com` (t≈45.3s), immediately followed by `media.megafilehub4.lat` (t≈45.8s), a fake file-hosting landing page.
2. **Payload fetch** — 10.1.21.58 then pulls a **16 MB** object from `arch.filemegahab4.sbs` (104.21.46.67:443, t≈48.4s) over TLS with ECH (SNI hidden as `cloudflare-ech.com`), consistent size for a stealer+loader bundle disguised as a downloadable archive. Content could not be inspected (encrypted).
3. **Browser fingerprinting / anti-sandbox gate** — starting t≈90–122s, the host repeatedly hits `whitepepper.su` (153.92.1.49) at `/api/set_agent`, sending a persistent per-victim `id` and `token`, and POSTing a full browser fingerprint (canvas hash, WebGL vendor/renderer, screen geometry, installed fonts, hardware concurrency, connection type, plugin list) to `.../api/set_agent?...&act=log`. The gate is queried once tagged `agent=Chrome` and again tagged `agent=Edge`, then serves a canned lure string `"cant open archive <hash>.zip"` before redirecting to `about:blank` — classic anti-bot/anti-analysis gating used to decide whether to serve the real payload to a genuine human browser.
4. **Further TDS hops** — `whooptm.cyou` (62.72.32.156), `holiday-forever.cc` (80.97.160.24), `communicationfirewall-security.cc` (104.21.9.36) are contacted in sequence after the fingerprint gate, consistent with a multi-hop traffic-distribution system chaining ad/verification redirects.
5. Immediately after this chain, the workstation generates an unusually large volume of **SAMR/LSARPC calls against the domain controller** (2,538 SAMR + 4,576 LSARPC frames, vs. normal light background AD chatter) — flagged as suspected post-infection AD/account enumeration, though this could not be independently attributed to the payload without process-level evidence and is reported as a behavioral flag, not a confirmed indicator.

All of these domains are newly-patterned, oddly-TLD'd (`.su`, `.sbs`, `.lat`, `.cyou`, `.cc`), Cloudflare-fronted infrastructure typical of malvertising/TDS-fronted stealer distribution — not naming a specific malware family with certainty since the payload itself was never observed in the clear.

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 / gate endpoints**
- `153.92.1.49:80` and `153.92.1.49:443` (whitepepper.su) — fingerprint-exfil / gate check-in, evidenced by frames 24500–25303 and repeated TLS SNI `whitepepper.su`

**Malicious/suspicious domains**
- `whitepepper.su` — fingerprinting/anti-bot gate, per-victim id/token check-in
- `arch.filemegahab4.sbs` (104.21.46.67, 172.67.136.13) — payload/archive download host
- `media.megafilehub4.lat` (104.21.48.156, 172.67.154.67) — fake file-hosting landing page
- `hiyter.com` (104.21.22.231, 172.67.207.145) — initial lure/redirector
- `whooptm.cyou` (62.72.32.156) — TDS redirector
- `holiday-forever.cc` (80.97.160.24) — TDS redirector
- `communicationfirewall-security.cc` (104.21.9.36, 172.67.141.109) — TDS redirector

**Malicious URLs**
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome`
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome&act=log` (POST, carries fingerprint exfil)
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Edge`
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Edge&act=log`

**File references**
- Bait filename served in the whitepepper.su lure text: `172.56.88.98-038485b1855ec7a1ba5bbda042ad17a1.zip`. This is a canned string embedded in the server's response text, not a file actually observed transferring to 10.1.21.58 — reported as bait text, not a confirmed dropped file.
- No file hash could be computed for the real payload: the 16 MB `arch.filemegahab4.sbs` download used TLS with Encrypted Client Hello and no session keys were available in this evidence set, so the object could not be carved or hashed.

## Benign Context (not indicators)
Microsoft NCSI (`www.msftconnecttest.com`), Windows/Office telemetry and login (`login.microsoftonline.com`, `login.live.com`, `settings-win.data.microsoft.com`, `odc.officeapps.live.com`), MSN/Bing content CDNs, Google services (`google.com`, `googleapis.com`, `gstatic.com`, `clients*.google.com`), `cdnjs.cloudflare.com`, `assets.adobedtm.com`, and all legitimate DHCP/NBNS/ARP/LDAP/Kerberos/SMB traffic between 10.1.21.58 and the domain controller 10.1.21.2.

## Summary
DESKTOP-ES9F3ML (10.1.21.58, MAC 00:21:5d:c8:0e:f2), logged in as domain user WIN11OFFICE\gwyatt, was infected after visiting a fake file-hosting site (hiyter.com → media.megafilehub4.lat) and downloading a 16 MB encrypted archive from arch.filemegahab4.sbs. The host subsequently checked in to a browser-fingerprinting gate at whitepepper.su using a persistent per-victim ID/token before hitting a chain of additional redirector domains, then generated abnormally heavy AD account-enumeration traffic against the domain controller. The malware family cannot be named with signature confidence — the behavior (fake-download lure, fingerprint-gated TDS chain, encrypted payload) matches known Lumma-Stealer-style ClickFix distribution patterns, but this is a behavioral assessment only.
